record.paper_title: Variation Structures: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Given two ε-hermitian variation structures, where such a structure for a group G is a quadruple (U;b,ρ,V) consisting of an ε-hermitian form b, a representation ρ:G->Aut(U;b), and a twisted homomorphism V:G->Hom(U*,U) satisfying θ^{-1}∘V(g)*=-εV(g)∘ρ(g)* and V(g)∘b=ρ(g)-I, how should their tensor product be defined in full generality? The answer should specify the resulting vector space, hermitian form, group representation, variation map, and sign convention, extending the known simple case in which the automorphism of the tensor product satisfies ⊗h=-εε1ε2 h1⊗h2.

evidence.quote: Definition. An ϵ–hermitian variation structure of the group G is a system V = (U ; b, ρ, V ) such that b is an ϵ–hermitian (maybe degenerate) form, ρ is a representation of G in Aut(U ; b), V is a twisted–homeomorphism, and they satify the following compatibility conditions for any g ∈ G: (i) θ−1 ◦ V (g)∗ = −ϵV (g) ◦ ρ(g)∗ , and (ii) V (g) ◦ b = ρ(g) − I.

If Vi , (i = 1, 2) are simple ϵi –hermitian variation structures, then the tensor product V1 ⊗ V2 deﬁnes a new simple ϵ–structure (for any ϵ). The corresponding automorphisms are related by ⊗ h = −ϵϵ1 ϵ2 h1 ⊗ h2 .
Problem # 2. Find the tensor product of two variation structures.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a group and let ε ∈ {+1, −1}. An ε-hermitian variation structure for G is a quadruple 𝒱 = (U; b, ρ, V) where:
• U is a finite-dimensional complex vector space (with dual U* and canonical isomorphism θ: U → U** given by θ(u)(φ) = \overline{φ(u)}),
• b: U → U* is an ε-hermitian (possibly degenerate) form, i.e. b* ∘ θ = ε b,
• ρ: G → Aut(U; b) is a group representation preserving b (so ρ(g)* ∘ b ∘ ρ(g) = b),
• V: G → Hom(U*, U) is a twisted homomorphism, i.e. V(gh) = V(g) + ρ(g) ∘ V(h) ∘ ρ(g)*,
subject to the compatibility conditions, for every g ∈ G:
 (i) θ^{-1} ∘ V(g)* = − ε V(g) ∘ ρ(g)*,
 (ii) V(g) ∘ b = ρ(g) − I_U.

Call 𝒱 simple if b is non-degenerate; in that case the associated automorphism is h := I + V ∘ b^{-1} (one h(g) for each g ∈ G, although in the simple case it is conventionally encoded by a single operator).

Known fact: if 𝒱_i = (U_i; b_i, ρ_i, V_i) (i = 1, 2) are simple ε_i-hermitian variation structures for G, then for any choice of sign ε ∈ {+1, −1} there is a tensor-product simple ε-hermitian variation structure 𝒱_1 ⊗ 𝒱_2 whose underlying space is U_1 ⊗ U_2, whose form is b_1 ⊗ b_2, whose representation is ρ_1 ⊗ ρ_2, and whose associated automorphism h satisfies
  h = − ε ε_1 ε_2 · (h_1 ⊗ h_2).

Problem. Extend this construction to the fully general (possibly degenerate) case: given two ε_i-hermitian variation structures 𝒱_i = (U_i; b_i, ρ_i, V_i) for G (i = 1, 2), define an ε-hermitian variation structure 𝒱_1 ⊗ 𝒱_2 = (U; b, ρ, V) for G, specifying:
• the underlying vector space U (presumably U_1 ⊗ U_2),
• the ε-hermitian form b on U,
• the representation ρ: G → Aut(U; b),
• the twisted homomorphism V: G → Hom(U*, U),
• the sign rule expressing ε in terms of ε_1, ε_2,
in such a way that (i) and (ii) are satisfied for every g ∈ G, and so that the construction reduces, in the simple case, to the formula above (h = − ε ε_1 ε_2 · h_1 ⊗ h_2).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return any source giving a general definition of the tensor product of (possibly degenerate) ε-hermitian variation structures, nor a paper announcing such a construction. The problem is explicitly posed as an open problem in the source list of problems, and no follow-up reference resolving it in full generality was located, so the current status is unverified.
